summary.headline: A tax-collecting cash machine that pays out everything, but the price already assumes a lot
summary.text: Ceylon Tobacco Company (CTC.N0000), 84% owned by British American Tobacco, sells almost all the legal cigarettes in Sri Lanka. It is a cash machine: no borrowings, Rs 28.8bn of cash, and every rupee of profit paid out as dividends (Rs 155.54 a share for 2025). But the government takes most of the price: levies were Rs 149.1bn of Rs 215.7bn turnover in 2025, and the income-tax rate rose from 40% to 45%, so profit fell 2% to Rs 29.1bn. January–September 2026 profit rose 5% to Rs 22.0bn (EPS Rs 117.28 against Rs 111.74), and three interim dividends of Rs 34, 41 and 41 have been declared. At Rs 1,788 (last trade on 30 September 2026, from the Q3 report) it trades at 11.1x trailing earnings with a dividend yield of about 9%. Four methods put fair value at about Rs 1,530, so the price is about 17% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 1,301 and treat under Rs 1,148 as a strong buy.

fullText:
Ceylon Tobacco Company (CTC.N0000), 84% owned by British American Tobacco, sells almost all the legal cigarettes in Sri Lanka. It is a cash machine: no borrowings, Rs 28.8bn of cash, and every rupee of profit paid out as dividends (Rs 155.54 a share for 2025). But the government takes most of the price: levies were Rs 149.1bn of Rs 215.7bn turnover in 2025, and the income-tax rate rose from 40% to 45%, so profit fell 2% to Rs 29.1bn. January–September 2026 profit rose 5% to Rs 22.0bn (EPS Rs 117.28 against Rs 111.74), and three interim dividends of Rs 34, 41 and 41 have been declared. At Rs 1,788 (last trade on 30 September 2026, from the Q3 report) it trades at 11.1x trailing earnings with a dividend yield of about 9%. Four methods put fair value at about Rs 1,530, so the price is about 17% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 1,301 and treat under Rs 1,148 as a strong buy.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
FCFE DCF | 1,041.3 | 1,350.0 | 1,773.2 | 1,342.0
P/E method | 1,350.0 | 1,760.0 | 2,184.0 | 1,721.8
Dividend model | 1,027.4 | 1,333.3 | 1,731.9 | 1,321.3
Dividend yield | 1,428.6 | 1,777.8 | 2,100.0 | 1,737.5
Average | 1,211.8 | 1,555.3 | 1,947.3 | 1,530.6

Why the price looks high: the market is pricing CTC as if a 13% return is enough. With a 16% cost of equity (10-year bond about 12.4% plus about 4 points for tax and excise risk) the cash-flow methods give about Rs 1,330–1,350; only the P/E and yield methods support today's price.

Expected return at Rs 1,788: dividend about 9% plus growth of about 4% gives about 13% a year, before any change in the share price's rating. That is above the bond yield but below the 16% I ask of a single-product business whose profit the government can change at each budget.

Buy plan: 200 shares up to Rs 1,530.60, 150 up to Rs 1,301.00 and 150 up to Rs 1,148.00, about Rs 673,470 in total (average Rs 1,346.94), against Rs 894,000 at Rs 1,788.

Business tests: 4 of 4 passed, so it's a good business at a high price: watch list (category 2).
